name: ABBA
hook: A Swedish group who won Eurovision in 1974, built a dense layered studio sound in Stockholm, and almost never let anyone sample them, until Madonna sent a letter.

blurb.age13: ABBA formed in Stockholm in 1972. Its four members were two couples: Agnetha Fältskog and Björn Ulvaeus, and Benny Andersson and Anni-Frid Lyngstad. Björn and Benny wrote the songs. In 1974 they won the Eurovision Song Contest with 'Waterloo', sung in English, and became one of the best-selling groups ever. Their engineer, Michael B. Tretow, stacked up many recordings of the same parts to make a huge, layered sound. They stopped in 1982. Björn and Benny almost never allow other musicians to sample their songs, but in 2005 Madonna sent someone to Stockholm with a letter asking to use 'Gimme! Gimme! Gimme!', and they said yes. In 2021 they released a new album, and since 2022 digital versions of them have performed concerts in London.
blurb.adult: Formed in Stockholm in 1972 by Agnetha Fältskog, Björn Ulvaeus, Benny Andersson and Anni-Frid Lyngstad, with Stig Anderson as manager and owner of their label, Polar Music. They won Eurovision in Brighton on 6 April 1974 with 'Waterloo'. Engineer Michael B. Tretow experimented with a layered wall-of-sound production that became their signature, and by 1978 they had turned a disused Stockholm cinema into their own Polar Music Studio. Both couples divorced during the group's later years, and several of the late songs are often heard as being about that. They stopped in December 1982. Andersson and Ulvaeus are known for refusing sample requests, which is what makes Madonna's 'Hung Up' (2005) unusual: it was cleared only after she sent a letter to Stockholm and they negotiated a large share of the royalties. They reunited for 'Voyage' (November 2021), and the 'ABBA Voyage' residency, performed by digital avatars, opened in London in May 2022.
